description: 2D SVG canvas with pan, zoom, grid overlay, and ruler bars. All coordinates in cm.
steps: Canvas renders with a cm grid (major lines every 5cm, minor every 1cm)
Scroll wheel zooms in/out (25%–400%); Ctrl+0 fits to screen
Middle-click drag or Space+drag pans the canvas
Ruler bars on top and left edges show cm values that update on pan/zoom
Grid toggles with Ctrl+G

description: Line tool (L): click start point → click end point to create a straight line segment.
steps: Pressing L activates line tool; cursor changes to crosshair
Click once to set start; click again to set end and commit the line
Line appears immediately on canvas at correct cm coordinates
Pressing Escape cancels in-progress line without committing

description: Curve tool (C): click start → drag control handle → click end to create a cubic bezier curve.
steps: Pressing C activates curve tool
Click start point, drag to set first control handle (tangent preview shown)
Click end point to commit curve
Curve renders as smooth bezier on canvas
Pressing Escape cancels in-progress curve

description: Select tool (S): click to select elements; drag to box-select; drag selected elements to move them.
steps: Clicking a line or curve highlights it with selection handles
Dragging across empty canvas draws a selection box; all elements inside become selected
Dragging a selected element moves it; coordinates update in real-time
Delete key removes selected elements
Clicking empty canvas deselects all

description: Snap system: endpoint, midpoint, grid, perpendicular, angle (Shift), and intersection snapping.
steps: Cursor within 8 screen pixels of an endpoint shows endpoint snap indicator and snaps to it
Cursor near midpoint of a line shows midpoint snap indicator
Grid snap locks cursor to nearest 0.5cm grid intersection when no other snap is active
Holding Shift constrains line direction to 0°, 45°, 90°, or 135°
Snap can be toggled off with Ctrl+Shift+S

description: Collapsible right-side panel where user enters body measurements (waist, hip, waist-to-hip, skirt length, bust, etc.).
steps: Panel lists all measurement fields with cm inputs
Values persist in app state across tool uses
Out-of-range values show inline validation error
Panel collapses/expands with a toggle button without disrupting the canvas

description: Line and curve length fields accept formulas referencing measurement variables (e.g., 'hip / 2 + 1'). Dimensions update when measurements change.
steps: Select a line; Properties panel shows a length field that accepts a formula string
Typing 'hip / 2 + 1' with hip=96 shows computed value 49 cm in real-time
Changing hip measurement to 100 updates all formulas that reference hip immediately
Invalid formula shows friendly error; line retains previous length
Formula is saved and restored with the .psnap file

description: Pattern piece management: close an outline to form a piece, name it, set cut quantity and fold line status.
steps: Snapping the last point of an outline to the first point closes it and fills it with a light color
Pressing Enter also closes the active outline
Closed piece can be named in the Properties panel
Cut quantity field (default: 2) and 'On fold' toggle available per piece
Cut quantity and name render as text inside the piece on the canvas

description: Seam allowance tool (A): generates an offset outline around a closed piece or along selected edges.
steps: Selecting a closed piece and pressing A prompts for allowance amount (default 1.5 cm)
Offset outline appears as a dashed line in a contrasting color
Edges marked as fold lines receive no seam allowance
Allowance amount is editable after creation via Properties panel

description: Transform closed pieces: drag-to-move, flip horizontal/vertical, and rotate by preset or custom angle — all transforms pivot around the piece centroid.
steps: Drag a selected piece fill to move all its segments together as a unit
Right-click piece fill → context menu shows Flip H, Flip V, Rotate 90° CW, Rotate 90° CCW, Rotate 180°
Properties panel shows Flip H / Flip V buttons and rotate preset buttons when a piece is selected
A custom angle input in the Properties panel rotates by an arbitrary degree value

description: Select individual sides of a closed piece; Delete key reverts the side (and the whole piece) to standalone segments; right-click a side for a context menu with Remove from Piece / Delete.
steps: Clicking a line or curve that belongs to a piece selects that segment
With a piece-side selected, pressing Delete reverts the entire piece to standalone segments (all segments freed, piece deleted)
Right-clicking a piece-side shows a context menu with 'Remove from piece' and 'Delete' options
Right-clicking the piece fill shows transform options (Flip H/V, rotate presets)

description: Grain line tool (G) and notch tool (N) for adding standard sewing pattern markings.
steps: G tool draws a double-arrow line labeled as grain direction
N tool adds a perpendicular tick mark on a line at the clicked position
Grain lines and notches are saved with the pattern piece
Both markings render in the SVG and PDF exports

description: Context-sensitive Properties panel showing editable attributes for the selected element (length/formula, coordinates, stroke, fold line toggle).
steps: Selecting a line shows: start/end coordinates, length, formula field, fold-line toggle
Selecting a curve shows: start/end/control point coordinates and length
Selecting a piece shows: name, cut qty, on-fold toggle, seam allowance
Editing a coordinate field moves the element endpoint in real-time

description: Full undo/redo stack for all editing actions (add, delete, move, property change).
steps: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action; element reverts to previous state
Ctrl+Y redoes the last undone action
Undo stack survives tool switches
Stack depth: at least 50 steps

description: Save pattern to .psnap JSON file (Ctrl+S) and load from .psnap (File → Open or drag-and-drop).
steps: Ctrl+S downloads a .psnap file containing all pieces, elements, formulas, and measurements
File → Open or dragging a .psnap onto the canvas restores the exact pattern state
Measurement values and parametric formulas are preserved on reload
Loading a file clears the current canvas and confirms with the user if there are unsaved changes

description: Export pattern as SVG with real-world cm viewBox, all markings, and a 5 cm test square.
steps: File → Export → SVG downloads a valid SVG file
ViewBox uses cm units so 1 SVG unit = 1 cm
All pieces, seam allowances, grain lines, notches, and labels are included
A 5 cm × 5 cm labeled test square appears in the output

description: Export tiled PDF (A4 or US Letter) with 1.5 cm page overlap, registration crosshairs, grid coordinates, and assembly diagram.
steps: File → Export → Tiled PDF (A4) generates a multi-page PDF
Adjacent pages overlap by 1.5 cm on shared edges
Crosshair registration marks appear in each overlap zone
Pages labeled with grid coordinates (A1, A2, B1, etc.)
First page contains an assembly diagram showing the page grid layout
5 cm test square present on first page; measures exactly 5 cm when printed at 100%

description: Export all pattern pieces on a single large-format PDF page (for plotters).
steps: File → Export → Single-Page PDF generates a PDF with page size matching the pattern bounding box
All pieces included with correct scale
5 cm test square included

description: Mirror a pattern piece horizontally or vertically to generate the opposite half.
steps: Select a closed piece; Edit → Mirror Horizontal creates a horizontally mirrored copy
Edit → Mirror Vertical creates a vertically mirrored copy
Mirrored piece is a new independent piece with a name suffixed ' (mirrored)'
Mirrored piece retains seam allowances, grain lines, and notches

description: All core tools and actions accessible via keyboard shortcuts as specified in the PRD.
steps: S, L, C, P, A, G, N, E activate their respective tools
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo/redo
Delete removes selected elements
Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- zoom in/out; Ctrl+0 fits to screen
Ctrl+G toggles grid; Ctrl+Shift+S toggles snap
Ctrl+S saves; Ctrl+N creates a new piece

description: Phase 2: Upload garment photo(s); backend calls Claude vision API and returns detected SkirtFeatures JSON.
steps: Upload modal accepts JPEG/PNG up to 10 MB; front photo required, back optional
POST /api/analyze returns SkirtFeatures JSON with silhouette, waistband, closure, darts, details, confidence
Loading state shown during analysis ('Analyzing your skirt...')
Low confidence (< 0.5) flagged with a warning banner
If no skirt detected, user-friendly error message shown

description: Phase 2: Feature review modal where user confirms or corrects AI-detected garment features before pattern generation.
steps: Modal shows detected silhouette (visual icon selector), waistband, closure, dart count, details
User can change any field via dropdowns or toggles
Confirm button proceeds to measurements step
Back button returns to photo upload

description: Phase 2: Backend generates an initial pattern from confirmed features + measurements using the Aldrich parametric engine; result loads into the editor.
steps: POST /api/generate accepts SkirtFeatures + Measurements; returns .psnap JSON
Generated pattern loads into the Phase 1 editor with all pieces named and seam allowances applied
User can edit any piece in the editor after generation
Supports straight, pencil, and a-line silhouettes at minimum

description: Phase 2: Python parametric pattern engine (geometry.py, skirts.py, modifiers.py) that converts measurements + features into .psnap pattern pieces.
steps: pytest tests/test_geometry.py passes (Point math, bezier, seam offset)
pytest tests/test_skirts.py passes (straight skirt base block with correct dart intake)
pytest tests/test_modifiers.py passes (pencil, a-line, gathered silhouette modifiers)
Engine serialises output as valid .psnap JSON
5 golden-file test skirts pass within ±2 mm tolerance
